title: HECM Reinstatement Restoration: Amount and Wait Credit
content:
**1. Booking.** On a Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM) loan, the reinstatement restoration is booked as one line restoration entry referencing the most recent prepaid portion posted on the loan as restoring nothing to the line, and that one entry covers every portion posted on the loan as restoring nothing to the line; a loan with no such portion has nothing to restore.

**2. Amount.** The reinstatement restoration is the portions counted, less the amount kept back, plus the wait credit, floored at 0.00 and rounded half up to the cent once, at the end. The wait credit is the total of every portion posted on the loan as restoring nothing to the line, multiplied by the wait credit rate, divided by 100, multiplied by the wait period.

**3. The cured case.** The cured maturity case is the case named by the loan's most recent cure confirmation notice in its Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases records; a loan has at most one open maturity case at a time, so its cure confirmation notices fall on different dates. Interest accruals and line growth credits each post once a month, so the most recent one is a single entry.

**4. Quantities.** The portions counted are the principal portions posted on the loan as restoring nothing to the line. The amount kept back is 0.00. The wait credit rate is the annual growth rate applied by the most recent line growth credit on the loan, or the note rate plus the plan's line growth spread when none has been credited. The wait period is the calendar days from the cured maturity case's closed date to the handling date, divided by 365, or 0 when the loan has no cured case.

**Worked figure (hypothetical inputs).**

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| portions restoring nothing: principal 3000.00, interest 1200.00, premium 800.00 | total 5000.00 |
| most recent line growth credit, annual rate | 6.000 percent |
| days from the cured case's closed date to the handling date | 73, so a wait period of 0.2 |
| wait credit: 5000.00 multiplied by 6.000, divided by 100, multiplied by 0.2 | 60.00 |
| restoration: 3000.00 less 0.00 plus 60.00 | 3060.00 |

With no line growth ever credited and a note rate of 5.500 percent on a plan with a 0.50-point spread, the wait credit rate would be 6.000 percent all the same.
